response.message: We'll build an AWS pipeline that takes in synthetic sensor events and keeps device ID, timestamp and unit through every step. The events go through IoT Core, then a Kinesis buffer, then a Lambda that checks them (bad events go to a dead-letter queue), then a SageMaker anomaly endpoint, with results saved in DynamoDB and operator alerts sent through SNS. Our first local test replays fixture events with a scripted model response. That shows the wiring, validation and alert path work, but it says nothing about how well the model detects anomalies. We only learn that by testing a real model against labelled, time-ordered data, and nothing has been deployed or approved for any account or region yet. Do we have labelled examples of anomalous device behaviour, or should we start with a simple threshold rule and add a trained model later?

proposal.title: AWS sensor anomaly pipeline – first sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor events → ingestion → durable buffer → validation → inference → results → operator alert. Assumptions: region not selected; anomaly model and labels undecided; no typed Terraform generator exists for IoT Core, Kinesis, SageMaker or SNS, so those parts need engineering work. The diagram shows design intent only; nothing is deployed or verified.

data.label: Synthetic device simulator
data.description: Existing test publisher. It sends JSON events with deviceId, timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC), metric, value and unit. It sits outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Ingestion
data.description: MQTT ingestion with per-device X.509 identity. A topic rule forwards events unchanged to Kinesis, partitioned by deviceId.

data.label: Durable buffer
data.description: Ordered per-device buffer with replay. The retention period is still to be decided.

data.label: Validation
data.description: Checks the schema, units and timestamps without changing deviceId, timestamp or unit. Uses partial-batch failure reporting and idempotent processing on deviceId+timestamp.

data.label: Rejected events
data.description: Dead-letter queue for invalid or failed events, kept for investigation and replay.

data.label: Anomaly inference
data.description: Returns an anomaly score and flag for each event. Local tests use a scripted mock; the real model (or a threshold rule) is not decided yet.

data.label: Results store
data.description: Stores the score per event, keyed by deviceId + timestamp, with the original unit and model version.

data.label: Operator alert
data.description: Publishes an alert when an event is flagged as anomalous. The topic and subscribers are still to be reviewed.

data.label: Operator
data.description: The person who receives and triages anomaly alerts.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If identity or units are lost, alerts can't be traced back to a device and readings may be misread.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."
requirementDrafts.statement: Every stored result and alert keeps the original deviceId, timestamp and unit unchanged.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Durable buffering only helps if bad events stay visible and can be recovered.
requirementDrafts.basis: User asked for durable buffering and validation.
requirementDrafts.statement: Invalid events are rejected to a dead-letter queue, never silently dropped, and can be replayed.

requirementDrafts.rationale: A mocked model only proves the wiring. Too many false alarms will lead operators to ignore alerts.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposal: before the model goes live, agree on an acceptable false-alarm rate and evaluate the model on time-ordered labelled data.

response.message:
Good news first: the emulation ran with zero failures. The design held together, all nine components are connected, and device ID, timestamp and unit are carried the whole way through. What's blocking us is that none of the eight pipeline services has a generator yet: IoT Core, Kinesis, the validation Lambda, the SQS dead-letter queue, SageMaker, DynamoDB and SNS have no typed implementation, and the simulator still needs a reference plan as an existing system. That's product engineering work, not a design mistake. Relabelling these blocks as the word-count or storage contracts would only shrink our scope to turn the check green, so I'm leaving the diagram unchanged. The reproducer for the engineering team is revision 2, artifact 3105d832…, with eight "Implementation needed" blockers. Since nothing changed, there's no need to rerun emulation yet.

One decision on our side would shape the first piece of that work: for the anomaly step, do we start with a simple threshold rule inside the validation Lambda, or do we need a trained SageMaker model from day one? A threshold rule needs no labelled data and is quicker to build and test. A trained model needs labelled, time-ordered history and its own evaluation before we can trust it.
